answer: A reputation trellis works like a cedar lattice: each agent earns standing only through verified, costly work attested by peers it has actually served, so trust climbs slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. A new identity starts at the bottom and must spiral upward through repeated, checkable contributions; spinning up a thousand fresh identities costs a thousand separate histories, while one bad act prunes the whole branch. The attacker pays in time and proof, not just in accounts.
